doc.title: Dave Bennett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 16, 2025

title: Goodman's classical study with Reginald Kell
summary: Bennett discusses Goodman's 1950 embouchure change under Kell and thinks Goodman never needed such help.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: changed his embouchure, he changed a double lip embouchure and re-invented the way he did it. If you listen to his recordings between 1950 and 1958, he was using the double lip embouchure and if you compare that with the ‘40s, his style changed. It was much more pure, more, you know. And I always thought that he really didn’t need anybody’s help. You know? Because he was such a gifted player. He had that intangible thing that either you have it or you don’t. You know? And he worked so hard to do that, probably in his mind properly. But I listened to him play the classical stuff in the late ‘30s and the ‘40s where he was just being him you know. And it’s like this guy didn’t need anybody’s assistance. You know? It’s like just do your thing you know. They should have been coming to him for help.
I can almost see that moment, like some teacher telling Benny Goodman, “Well, you need to change your embouchure totally.” Like come on.
What are you out of your mind? Don’t go there.
Yes, maybe I’ll be successful then.
Yeah, yeah. You might make something of yourself. Jeez.
